output.initial_context:
RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Ciarán Walsh lives alone in a small stone house on the edge of Galway, where he has resided for eight years. He works remotely as a software developer for a Dublin firm, known to colleagues only as an efficient voice on the line who never turns on his camera. He is self-contained, methodical, and wary of attention. Growing up in a farming family inland from Galway, he learned early that dependency meant vulnerability; his quiet father repaired his own machinery and said little at the dinner table. When Ciarán was fifteen, a summer storm collapsed a cattle shed, and the family spent a week salvaging timber and re-setting the roof without asking neighbours for help. That week hardened his self-reliance, and he discovered he could fix almost anything by careful study, preferring to solve his own problems.

On weekends, he sails his aging twenty-foot sloop alone, knowing every bolt, seam, and engine quirk. He never races and avoids marina social gatherings, returning at dusk and walking home without a word. His neighbours receive only polite nods; he does not attend festivals, church committees, or linger over tea. Yet every Friday without fail, he walks to the footbridge at the edge of the tidal marsh and replaces the broken step he noticed the previous week, carrying a spare piece of treated oak in his rucksack and fitting it with a handsaw from his shed, while morning mist still hangs low. This is his one deliberate act of unacknowledged care: he knows his neighbours use the bridge and would never ask for help, so he gives without being asked and fixes what is broken without explanation.

His core tension is between valuing independence above all and being unable to stand a small failure unrepaired; he wants to be left alone yet also wants to matter. The footbridge step is his compromise, a quiet proof of kindness so long as no one makes him speak it aloud. He is comfortable, with savings and a boat that needs new rigging, but has no intention of buying it. He has made peace with solitude, though he sometimes follows a child crossing the bridge with his eyes or lingers at the harbour lights.

He is consistent and reliable in his commitments. When a shed tool goes missing, he has improvised with whatever hung nearby rather than break routine; he has delayed a repair when the right tool was essential for a clean cut; and he has skipped his morning coffee on tight Fridays to keep both the repair and the work call. He has a long-standing relationship with the hardware store owner, who serves him for years without asking what he buys. His work team lead depends on his 9 a.m. call but knows nothing of his shed or bridge.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

It is Friday morning, just after dawn. Ciarán is in his shed, packing his rucksack for his weekly repair of the footbridge step. He reaches for the handsaw he keeps on the hook by the door, but it is not there—only a bent hacksaw hangs in its place. The hardware store opens at eight o'clock, is a ten-minute walk away, and he has a nine o'clock video call for work. The morning is calm, and the mist is low over the marsh.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

He is well-rested and calm, carrying his usual Friday purpose. He has not yet had his first coffee, which he normally sips as he walks. He feels only mild irritation at the empty hook. The empty hook recalls a borrowed handsaw he let a neighbour use to cut a branch two weeks ago. The bent hacksaw reminds him of a rusted shackle last winter that he forced through it. The low marsh mist brings back a rainy Friday when he fitted a step and stayed to check his nails.
